summary: Feed s123_double to IDS is degraded: 50% of traffic missing VLAN 20 tags and microbursts peak at 1.82 Gbps (182% of 1 Gbps port) causing overload. Both faults create blind spots for IDS detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or upstream SPAN/TAP trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or not trunking VLAN 20. 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 is completely absent despite IDS requiring VLANs 10 and 20, indicating broker VLAN filtering / tag stripping misconfiguration.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to all traffic on VLAN 20 and cannot apply VLAN-aware signatures or segmentation policies; 50% untagged traffic loses tenant/context, reducing detection coverage for lateral movement between VLAN 10/20.

recommended_fix.why: Restore 802.1Q tags end-to-end so IDS receives both required VLANs 10 and 20 with tags intact for correct classification.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate traffic microbursts of 1.82 Gbps exceed the IDS 1 Gbps port capacity (182% load across 9 intervals). Packet broker is forwarding line-rate bursts without load-balancing, policing, or aggregation to match tool capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffer overruns and silently drops packets during bursts; with needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions=true, dropped packets break stream reassembly and signature matching, causing missed exploits and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 2+ IDS ports (or upgrade to 10G) with 5-tuple hashing to keep flows intact and keep per-port load below 80% threshold, preventing drops while preserving full payload for IDS.
